chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is not befitting to drink from vessels of gold or silver.

key_terms.آنِيَة: Vessels, utensils, dishes used for eating and drinking
key_terms.الذَّهَب: Gold — precious metal whose use in dinnerware is forbidden
key_terms.الْفِضَّة: Silver — precious metal equally prohibited for eating and drinking vessels
key_terms.لَا يَنْبَغِي: It is not befitting/appropriate — a jurisprudential formula expressing prohibition

ai.seo_question: Is it forbidden to drink from gold or silver vessels in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declared that drinking from gold or silver vessels is not permissible. This ruling falls within the broader Islamic prohibition on using gold and silver utensils, which scholars have understood as a means to discourage extravagant display of wealth and to promote equality and modesty in daily life. The original audience — students of Shia jurisprudence — would have understood this as a legally binding prohibition (haram), aligning with parallel rulings in the Sunni tradition as well.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companion, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at Bin Mihran, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘It is not befitting, drinking in a vessel of the gold and the silver’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah ibn Mehran who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is not proper to drink water with bowl made of gold or silver.’”
